correctness.rationale: PASS: Harmonic quadratics are complex symmetric trace-free matrices. Sign changes of transverse coordinates and their permutations force block orthogonality and scalar forms on Z(dim1), M(dim d-1), O(dim C(d-1,2)), D(dim d-2). The x1-positive condition halves the integrals since squared quadratic harmonics are even in global antipodal sign. For Gaussian G, Y_i=G_i² iid chi-square(1); condition on rank r of Y1=t and k=r-1 exceeders to derive rho, truncated moment a_j,b_j, conditional m,v,p,q. Recomputed representative denominators: E[(nY1-S)^2]=2d(d-1), E[G1²G2²]=1, E[G2²G3²]=1, E[(Y2-Y3)^2]=4. Each rank area 1/(2d), partitions hemisphere; trace and sum_r lambda=1/2 follow. Nonzero harmonics cannot vanish on an open cell, so for nonempty proper J, 0<lambda<1/2. Independent 500,000-sample d=4,r=2 Gaussian test approximates eigenlevels (0.02387,0.17418,0.07297,0.17443) near formula values (0.02368,0.17566,0.07434,0.17566). Monte Carlo is corroboration, not proof for all d.
